steps.label: Point mutation defined
steps.margin_note: Definition plus the other name. Three lines.
lines: A POINT MUTATION is a mutation that occurs in a
SINGLE BASE PAIR of a DNA fragment.
It is also called a gene mutation.
steps.why: Because only one base changes, the effect can be traced to one amino acid — which is what makes point mutations so well understood.
common_mistakes: Saying it changes a whole chromosome. That is a CHROMOSOMAL mutation.
Saying it changes several genes. It changes ONE base pair.
steps.memory_tip: One point on the DNA, one base pair.

steps.label: Example
steps.margin_note: Name the disease and the substitution. Six lines.

lines.text: Sickle cell anaemia: one base, one amino acid

steps.why: One base changing one amino acid changing the shape of a whole cell is the clearest chain from DNA to phenotype in the syllabus.
common_mistakes: Naming Down's syndrome. That is a CHROMOSOMAL mutation, not a point mutation.
Giving the name with no detail. The amino acid substitution is what makes it an example rather than a label.
steps.memory_tip: One letter changed, and the cell changes shape.
